question.leadin: Identify these longtime Senators who died in 2009 or 2010.
question.text: This longest-serving Senator in U.S. history represented West Virginia in the Senate from 1959 until his death in 2010.
question.clue: This long-serving West Virginian senator who once gave a 14-hour speech to filibuster the 1964 Civil Rights Act.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about a candidate in the 2016 Republican primaries.
swap.text: In a rally supporting Trump, this Tea Party politician called her supporters "proud clingers," a phrase which briefly went viral after her speech.
swap.clue: During her term as governor, she dealt with the "bridge to nowhere" incident, and dismissed Walt Monegan, her public safety commissioner.

question.text: The Saturday Night Massacre was completed when Nixon made this third man the acting Attorney General and got him to fire Cox. In 1987, President Reagan nominated this man to the Supreme Court, but the Senate voted him down.
question.clue: This man, who complied in firing Archibald Cox during the Saturday Night Massacre, was the focus of a committee hearing, led by Joe Biden, that decided not to replace Lewis Powell with this man.

swap.leadin: Name this people involved in the debate over the March 2010 passage of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act.
swap.text: This Speaker of the House was able to round up enough votes to get the bill through the House by a 219-212 vote.
swap.clue: This California Democrat is the first female Speaker of the House.

question.leadin: This senator shocked his fellow Republicans by voting against the Health Care Freedom Act, which was intended to replace the Affordable Care Act.
question.text: Name this Republican Senator from Arizona who passed away in August, 2018. In 2008, he ran unsuccessfully for the presidency against Barack Obama.
question.clue: At one campaign stop, this man was booed for correcting an audience member who called his opponent, Barack Obama, an Arab.

swap.leadin: Name some politicians from a state that just ain't the same since Strom Thurmond died, South Carolina.
swap.text: Known for telling staff he was on the Appalachian trail, while actually in Argentina with a mistress, this Republican governor of South Carolina has not been impeached despite threats from state legislators.
swap.clue: Upon his disappearance, aides to this South Carolina governor told the press he was busy "hiking the Appalachian trail." In fact, he was visiting his self-described soul-mate in Argentina.

question.leadin: This election's eventual winner emerged victorious following the Supreme Court's overturning of a prior ruling requiring a recount in Florida.
question.text: Name this election decided following the Court's ruling in Bush v. Gore.
question.clue: An international custody case involving the return of a boy to his father in Havana may have affected the outcome of this election in a place where the use of "butterfly ballots" helped Pat Buchanan overperform.

swap.text: This Baptist minister founded the Moral Majority in 1979, which had a major influence on the 1980 election. He also founded Liberty University.
swap.clue: This televangelist and founder of the Thomas Road Baptist Church in Lynchburg, Virginia. He died in 2007 and was also a major leader of the Moral Majority.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about presidential powers.
question.text: This power, granted to the president in 1996 but ruled unconstitutional in 1998, allowed him to omit specific spending requirements from a budget bill without killing the bill in its entirety.
question.clue: This power, by which the executive could disapprove some parts of a bill but leave others intact.

swap.text: The sole Republican candidate, he still trails O'Brien in the polls as the residency crisis is resolved.

question.text: During the 1964 election, this conservative wrote the pro-Goldwater book A Choice, Not an Echo. This activist founded the Eagle Forum and was noted for her opposition to the Equal Rights Amendment.
question.clue: This person likened "using an atomic bomb to exterminate mice" to legislation sponsored by Michigan representative Martha Griffiths.

swap.text: This woman founded StudentsFirst in order to help reform the education system. This former chancellor of the Washington DC school system also founded The New Teacher Project.
swap.clue: She called the election of Vincent Gray "devastating for the schoolchildren of D.C." after leading the district to an increase of 17 percentage points in math aptitude during her tenure.

question.leadin: In May 2017 this man issued an apology to the Chobani Yogurt Company for his allegation that a plant of that company was involved in a child abuse ring and was responsible for rises in tuberculous cases.
question.text: Name this far right-wing radio host and conspiracy theorist, known for spreading his views through InfoWars.com. This man claims that Donald Trump personally called him the day after being elected to thank him for his campaign efforts.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about political scandals in the 1980s.
swap.text: This Senator from Colorado withdrew his campaign for the Democratic nomination shortly after photos were released of him and Donna Rice on a yacht named Monkey Business.
swap.clue: In his first campaign for his party's nomination, his opponent quoted a Wendy's commercial in asking him "Where's the beef?"

question.leadin: This case applied the Lemon test to override the idea that the Louisiana law in question was attempting to protect academic freedom.
question.text: Name this 1986 establishment clause case which overturned a law forcing creation science to be taught alongside evolution.
question.clue: This 1987 Supreme Court case ruled that a Louisiana law requiring the teaching of creation science was unconstitutional because it was meant to advance religion. Either the plaintiff or defendant is acceptable.

swap.leadin: Name some people who, as of the writing of this bonus in early October, were Republican candidates for President.
swap.text: This Senator, who is widely rumored to be gay, has remained low in the polls but was widely regarded as the winner of the September 16th "kid's table" debate.
swap.clue: In a tweet, this South Carolina senator stated that "any policy proposal which drives up costs of Corona, tequila, or margaritas is a big-time bad idea" in response to a 20% income tax with Mexico to pay the wall.

question.leadin: Answer the following about writings on genocide and civil war.
question.text: This woman wrote A Problem from Hell about American foreign policy on genocides in the 20th century. She was the U.S. Ambassador to the UN from 2013 to 2017.

swap.leadin: The first effort to sequester the federal budget was instituted by an act named for this senator, Warren Rudman, and Fritz Hollings.
swap.text: Name this Texas senator, the first namesake of a 1999 act that overturned part of the Glass-Steagall Act, which he sponsored with Jim Leach and Thomas Bliley.

question.leadin: The winning candidate in this election made such bloopers as saying that Pearl Harbor occurred on September 7 and that he stood for "anti-Semitism." Answer the following about the election of 1988.
question.text: Possibly the most exciting moment in the campaign occurred in the vice-presidential debates when this Dukakis running mate and Texas Senator sneered that Dan Quayle was "no Jack Kennedy."
question.clue: He became president of Lincoln Consolidated during a fifteen-year absence from politics, which ended when he defeated George Bush in a 1970 election for senator from Texas.

swap.text: Although viewed by conservatives as a right-wing vote, Souter voted with the majority in this case, which ruled that schools could not sponsor clerics in even non-denominational prayers. This case dealt with a rabbi delivering a prayer at a graduation ceremony.
